[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | A cited line asks for mercy, and the dual expression ḥanānik appears in a verse by Ṭarafa; Ibn Qutayba traces the word to a she-camel's care for its young.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن الأنباري | reports | He says linguists agree ḥanān means mercy, and God did this out of mercy for Yaḥya's parents and to purify him.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · مجاهد | reports | A second view defines ḥanān as God's tenderness toward Yaḥya.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r7] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | He defines ḥanān as gentleness; another report from him gives blessing.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r8] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · عكرمة وابن زيد | reports | They define ḥanān as love.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p213/r9] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · عطاء بن أبي رباح | reports | He defines ḥanān as exaltation or reverence.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الخليل | reports | Ḥanān derives from yearning and distress at separation, like a camel's cry for its young; the Prophet's former palm trunk also moaned when he moved to the pulpit.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · بعضهم | reports | Some permit calling God al-Ḥannān in the sense of the compassionate and merciful.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · منهم | reports | Others disallow the divine name because of the word's original associations and because no reliable report establishes it among God's names.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p163#2/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | If ḥanān describes God, one reading says He gave Yaḥyā judgment and mercy toward him, with zakāh as purification and honor.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p164#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Calling Yaḥyā's purity a gift from God supports the view that God creates human acts; explaining it as mere enabling grace departs from the apparent wording.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p164#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Pious means both avoiding what God forbids and not neglecting what He commands; it is the highest praise and describes Yaḥyā, who neither sinned nor intended sin.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | If divine ḥanān is for Zakariyyā, God says He answered his prayer by giving him a son and then granted that son judgment and mercy, purifying Zakariyyā from being a rejected supplicant.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r10] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Zakāh may also mean blessing and growth.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | If divine ḥanān is for Yaḥyā's community, God bestowed judgment and mercy on him for his people's benefit through his guidance.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | If ḥanān describes Yaḥyā, it means tenderness toward people coupled with purity from neglecting obligations, since kindness can otherwise lead one to excuse wrongdoing.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The account also allows that Yaḥyā never sinned or even intended sin; Qur'anic commands to show gentleness and severity together illustrate why purity must constrain mercy.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · عطاء بن رباح | reports | ʿAṭāʾ ibn Rabāḥ interprets ḥanān as honor: Waraqa tells those torturing Bilāl that if they kill him he will honor him, as a parallel use.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك وابن جريج | reports | They interpret zakāh as a righteous, pure deed.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الحسن | reports | Al-Ḥasan says Yaḥyā's zakāh made those who accepted him pure as well.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r8] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Another interpretation says God purified Yaḥyā by praise, as witnesses' testimony purifies a person.
[RAZI-FULL:v21p164/r9] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الكبي | reports | Al-Kalbī says Yaḥyā was a charitable gift that God bestowed on his parents.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عكرمة | reports | Ikrima interprets hannan as love; the cited poetic usage also describes spouses’ affection.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Zakat here means purification, blessing, and growth in good works, making Yahya a blessing who guides people.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن قتيبة | reports | Ibn Qutayba offers the alternative that Yahya was a charitable gift to his parents.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Yahya was obedient to God and therefore neither committed a sin nor inclined toward one.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عبد الله بن عمرو | reports | A report from the Prophet says every child of Adam comes on Judgment Day with a sin except Yahya ibn Zakariyya; Qurtubi gives no grading here.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو عبيدة | reports | Abu Ubayda says Arabs use hananak or hananayk, O Lord, to mean Your mercy, as in the cited Imru al-Qays poem.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r11] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari takes hannan as mercy, tenderness, and compassion for Yahya’s parents and others.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r12] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن الأعرابي | reports | Ibn al-A‘rabi distinguishes divine Hannan with a doubled n, meaning Merciful, from hannan with a light n, meaning tenderness and mercy; he also records provision and blessing as senses.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r13] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عطية | reports | Ibn Atiyya records hannan as something sacred or exalted in God, citing Zayd ibn Amr’s vow to make Bilal’s grave a place of devotion; al-Harawi and al-Azhari gloss the story as compassion for him.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r14] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | Qurtubi concludes that hannan means tenderness, in agreement with Mujahid, whether the tenderness is from God toward Yahya or from Yahya toward creation.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says Yahya never committed or even contemplated a sin, great or small, and never desired a woman.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says Yahya ate grass and had permanent channels for tears in his cheeks.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Qurtubi refers back to his discussion of Yahya as master and chaste in the account of Zakariyya. | mentions 3:39
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Hannan is grammatically coordinated with judgment.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says he does not know what hannan means.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · جمهور المفسرين | reports | Most commentators understand hannan as compassion, mercy, and love, an act of the inner self.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · النحاس | reports | Al-Nahhas transmits two Ibn Abbas explanations: God’s compassionate mercy toward Yahya, or the mercy Yahya was given toward people to rescue them from unbelief and idolatry.
[QURTUBI-FULL:19:13/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The word derives from a she-camel’s yearning over its young; hananak and hananayk are either synonymous forms or a dual form.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:19:13-15/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Divine ḥanān is mercy toward Yahya or tenderness in his heart toward his parents and others; zakāh is purity from sins, God's charitable gift to his parents, or his being enabled to affirm people. He was obedient and avoided sin.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Ḥanān means compassion and mercy toward his parents and others, and is coordinated with الحكم.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | From Our presence means from God; zakāh means purity and righteousness, and Yahya did not deliberately commit sin.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#5/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | He was devout, Muslim, and obedient.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p216#2/r8] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The syntax joins hannan to the gift of wisdom; God gave wisdom and affection and made Yahya pure; hannan is loving compassion like a camel's tenderness for its young.
